To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in WDTC patients treated in Boston by thyroidectomy and radioablation, tumor size and gender are not predictive of persistence and/or recurrence, but age at diagnosis is.

in patients with WDTC who underwent total or near total thyroidectomy with or without radioiodine treatment, neither tumor size nor male gender contribute significantly to disease persistence/recurence, and that age at initial surgery has some positive prognosttic value.

in well-differentiated (papillary and/or follicular) thyroid carcinoma patients treated by thyroidectomy with or without radioiodine therapy, tumor size, gender and histology are not predictive of persistence or recurrence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the persistence/recurrence of well-differentiation thyroid carcinoma, and not the extent of the primary tumor or the lymph node involvement.

the identification of factors that may be predictive of WDTC persistence or recurrence in patients treated by surgery and radioiodine, without consideration of local or regional extent of the disease.
the identification of prognostic factors for the persistence/recurrence of well-differentiate thyroid cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in the absence of local, loco-regional and distant disease extent, neither size of the tumor nor gender contribute to persistence/recurrence, and that age at diagnosis has a positive prognostic impact.
the size of the tumor is of little prognostic value in the absence of local, loco-regional, and distant disease.
tumor size and gender are not predictive of WDTC persistence or recurrence in patients treated with total or near total thyroidectomy with or without radioiodine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in WDTC, persistence/recurrence is not predicted by gender, ethnicity, tumor histology, or multifocality.

, in patients with well differentiated thyroid carcinoma, the extent of the disease (local, regional and distant) and the histotype (papillary or follicular) have a major role in the outcome of the disease.

, in WDTC patients treated with total or near total thyroidectomy followed by radioiodine and without consideration of the local, locoregal, and distant extent, tumor size and gender do not contribute to disease persistence or recurrence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for patients with WDTC treated by total and/or near total thyroidectomy, the presence of a single focus of disease is not associated with a higher risk of disease recurrence/persistence.
the risk of persistence/recurrence is not related to gender, ethnicity, tumor histology, or tumor size.
the risk of recurrence in patients with well-differentiated cancer treated by total thyroidectomy is very low.
